value.rationale: The exact minimum reciprocal intervention cost and complete set/count of equally inexpensive interventions give a meaningful structural repair policy for a natural sparse directed public-goods game, not a routine arbitrary instance. The sharp sparse-network existence decay and bounded expected multiplicity quantify the stochastic reliability of specialists and contrast with dense-network equilibrium existence. Both questions are motivated by the original game-theoretic model and a useful economic intervention operation.
